Settings

⏰ Daily 15 minutes

One nudge a day, at a time you pick. The app knows whether anything counted as studying today — if something did, it stays quiet.
A web page cannot ring a phone that is closed. The calendar button saves a repeating 15-minute event with an alarm into your calendar app — that one rings every day whether the app is open or not.

This list is the syllabus. Move a chapter to match the order your school teaches it, rename one, delete one you don't need, or add your own. Everything else follows this list.

Study plan

Three phases run from today to the exam. The dates come from your exam date — change the name, the length, or how hard the app pushes in each one.

NCERT textbooks

The official books, free and legal from NCERT's own site. Open any chapter directly from the Book tab — every chapter links to its exact PDF.
Read NCERT alongside this app, not instead of it. NEET Chemistry — especially inorganic — is set from NCERT's exact wording. Nothing else matches it.

How this works

📖 What this app is, and isn't ▾
It is: a study system. Chapter lessons written for the exam, a practice engine that finds your weak spots, flashcards scheduled by a real memory model, and mock tests with honest analysis.

It is not: a replacement for the NCERT textbooks, or for solving problems with a pen. No app is. The lesson for a chapter is roughly 3 pages; the NCERT chapter is roughly 25. Use both.
📇 The flashcard scheduler ▾
Uses FSRS, the same algorithm Anki adopted. It tracks per-card stability and difficulty, and works out the probability you'd recall a card right now. Cards come back exactly when you're about to forget — which is when review is cheapest. Rate honestly: marking something "Easy" when you half-knew it is the fastest way to break the whole system.
🎯 Why explanations come last ▾
A 1,000-student study found students given an always-on AI chatbot scored +48% while using it — then 17% worse than students who never had AI once it was taken away. A tutor that withheld answers and gave hints got +127% with almost no damage.

So this app will not give you the answer first. Attempt → hint → explanation. That ordering is the difference between learning and outsourcing.
🔍 The five error types ▾
Wrong answers are classified from your speed, your confidence tap, and your history:

📕 Knowledge gap — wrong, slow, never studied it → go read the chapter.
⏳ Forgotten — you knew it, it faded → review today.
🧠 Misconception — wrong and confident, repeatedly → re-learn the concept, not the fact.
🎯 Careless — wrong, very fast, you were sure → process fix, not more studying.
⏱️ Too slow — right, but 3× the time → timed drills.

Most students think they lose marks to ignorance when they actually lose them to the last two.
📊 Score band, and why it's a band ▾
A single number would be a lie. The band widens when you've taken few tests and narrows as you take more. Every test logs predicted-vs-actual in Progress → Calibration.
🔧 The tutor's key ▾
The app ships with a working free key, so there is nothing for you to set up. You only need this if you are looking after the app and want a different key.
⚠️ Honest limits ▾
Lessons: all 50 chapters of the NEET syllabus are written — around 69,500 words, which is about a third of the NCERT word count. Depth, not coverage, is where this is thin.
Question bank: 360 built-in — Physics 90, Chemistry 90, Biology 180, plus 114 fully worked examples. Two full NEET-length mocks in a row share no questions. Still a foundation, not a syllabus: grow it chapter by chapter.
AI explanations can be wrong. Trust NCERT over the app whenever they disagree. Tap 🚩 to report a bad question.
Diagrams: 41 are drawn in, across 21 chapters, as their own part of each chapter. NCERT has hundreds, so still read the book alongside — the graphs and plots for Chemistry and Physics are the thinnest.
The tutor's free budget: the built-in key gets about 50 free requests a day and resets at midnight UTC (5:30 am India). Run out and the tutor goes quiet for the rest of the day — nothing else in the app is affected, and no data is lost.
Built for one student. Good luck. 🩺
